C144.notes: SER EU-NO-001. Obverse crowned Harald V monogram · legend 50 ØRE · NORGE · 1998 · crossed hammers · user shorthand 1998 + photo · Joseph: Here’s what I pick for 1500. Copper-toned Nordic odd-unit from the late 90s — café / kiosk / ferry change while the øre still jingled, fourteen years before the 50 øre was pulled from circulation in 2012. Country #21 — first Norway in the vault. Soft beat 1500 locks on this piece. Year-after sibling C268 / EU-NO-002 (2000 50 Øre · same KM#460 Nidhogg type). Norway flips now 2.
C144.story: A 1998 50 øre from Norway. The obverse shows crowned Harald V monogram + crossed-hammers mintmark; the reverse shows Nidhogg dragon (Urnes stave-church portal); 50 ØRE, NORGE (1998) / NOREG (2000), date, engraver GJL (Grażyna Jolanta Lindau). Struck in bronze (97% Cu · 2.5% Zn · 0.5% Sn).

C268.notes: SER EU-NO-002. Photo confirmed (Joseph: year crop clearly 2000 · reverse in white 2×2) · user cue Norway 50 Øre 2000 · bronze circulated · dull brown toning. Reverse Nidhogg (Urnes portal dragon) · legend 50 ØRE · NOREG · 2000 · small mark by the motif is engraver GJL (Grażyna Jolanta Lindau) — not the mintmark; crossed hammers + mintmaster JEJ (Jan Erik Johansen) sit on the unshown crown obverse (Kongsberg / Royal Norwegian Mint). Same KM#460 bronze type as year-before sibling C144 / EU-NO-001 (1998 50 Øre · vault-1500 soft beat · country #21) — different year, keep both. Millennium-year Nordic odd-øre — café / kiosk / ferry change while the 50 øre still jingled, twelve years before demonetization on 1 May 2012 (Norges Bank / Numista). Norway flips now 2.
